name: Standby generator

combustion.note: Run it only outdoors, never in a garage, shed or other closed space: the exhaust carries carbon monoxide. kW is the gas a 22 kW Generac burns, natural gas at half load up to propane at full load; larger and diesel sets burn more.

comps.spec: Generator head, 10–25 kW on home units, hundreds of kW on commercial sets
Air-cooled V-twin on home units; large liquid-cooled engines on commercial sets
12V starting battery (24V on large diesel sets)

comps.loc: Grey box beside the main electrical panel

comps.spec: Output breaker and transfer switch breakers
Diesel in a base or day tank, 100–4,000 L (diesel sets)
Large propane tank, roughly 400–4,000 L (propane-fed sets; natural gas units have none) — decanting needs proper fittings
comps.loc: Buried or on a pad near the generator

comps.spec: Weatherproof steel or aluminium enclosure panels

notes:
Too heavy to move, but it runs where it stands: the fuel, transfer switch and battery are the quick wins. Open the main breaker to the grid before running it so it can't backfeed the lines.

A 22 kW Generac home unit (21 kW on natural gas) burns about 6.3–9.3 m³ of natural gas an hour at half to full load and turns only about 16–22% of it into electricity (Generac 22 kW; NRCan Heating with Gas): run the furnace and well pump from it, not electric heaters.

sources.title: Generac 22 kW: Generac, Guardian 22kW home standby generator (model 7042), product page and specifications
